beats.display_text: Idea one comes from Jason Fried's Write_On. Not version control, but alternative control.
Version control thinks in time: snapshots of the whole document, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday. To find an old phrasing, you dig through the past.
Alternative control thinks in place. The other ways of saying this one line live right underneath it.
Put the caret on a word and press Ctrl+Shift+A. Now that word can hold variants.
Hover and press the arrow keys, and you read each option in context, in the sentence where it has to live.
It works at three sizes, which Write-on calls grains. A word gets a thin violet wave. A sentence, a lower rose wave. A paragraph, a copper bar in the margin.
And flipping between variants is not an edit. Nothing is lost, and there's nothing to undo.
